item.content:encoded: I used the app, yes. My French is nonexistent, I am only really reading fluent in German (and English). That's an obvious error though, that I should have expected and corrected for. Still the information was good, and my conclusion was correct.

item.title: Re: IMAGE PROVENANCE
item.content:encoded:
Oh dear — you used Google Translate, didn't you.

For the record, the photographer's name was "Daniel Rouillé" — "rouillé" being French for "rusty", of course. Mr Rouillé died in 1920, and all his photographs are public domain by now. It's still good to keep track of provenance, though.

item.title: Re: IMAGE PROVENANCE
item.content:encoded:
the original photo is probably public domain by now.

That photo appears to be part of the collection of Gustave Soury (d. 1966), and was given to him by photographer Daniel Rouillé (probably deceased) around 1900, so therefore taken between 1880 and 1900.

This pdf describes the collection.

item.title: IMAGE PROVENANCE
item.content:encoded:
Image's proximate source:

https://www.flickr.com/photos/49879584@N00/4388753827

which is apparently a photo taken by Flickr user "DoubleM", of a photo in the Musée des Civilisations de l'Europe et de la Méditerranée (Museum of Civilizations of Europe and the Mediterranean), in Marseilles, France. The photo's original metadata is presumably on file in the Museum. DoubleM licensed his (her?) photo as Creative Commons (Attribution Required); the original photo is probably public domain by now.

I dislike the use of the term "Eldritch" in anything and everything SCP-universe related….

…but that said this did a great job of giving us a vision of both what the circus is like and of at least part of its true nature. Horrifying and wonderful. A video version of this would be more than slightly unsettling to watch.
